The Rebbe notes: 'yesh derech acher, bechinat derech isha mena'efet.' This is the evil mirror of Package 1 (the holy derech/isha nexus). The pgam habrit produces precisely this distortion — the 'path' becomes the 'way of the adulteress.' This evil bechina is mentioned explicitly in the Torah text but is not a separate node in the dataset; it is embedded within the proof text of the אשה↔דרך edge.

additions.reason: The Torah identifies 224 (rach'd) lights as the content that must shine in the 'yam' (sea) which is emunah. These 224 lights are a distinct concept — the specific divine light-content of the Elul kavvanot — and they are in bechina relation to the yam/emunah complex (they constitute what the sea/emunah holds). While the Rebbe does not use the explicit word 'bechina' here, the identification is structural: 'haya tzarich leha'ir bechinat harach'd orot bivchinат yam, bechinat emunah.' The 224 lights are what the yam/emunah is meant to contain and radiate.

structural_notes: This is a very short Torah (9 lines). The dataset correctly captures the two central bechina pairs. The eitza edges (kavvanat Elul → tikkun habrit → finding one's zivug) are properly classified as eitza and are not included in the bechina subgraph.

The Torah has an implicit good/evil mirror: Package 1 (אשה/דרך) is neutral because the same isha-derech nexus appears in both holy form (the legitimate wife, the tikkun) and evil form ('derech isha mena'efet'). The evil form is named in the text but not as a separate dataset node.

Package 2 (ים/אמונה) has no explicit evil mirror in this Torah — the Rebbe does not discuss a 'sea of evil' or 'corrupted faith' dimension here. The focus is entirely on the positive, corrective domain.
The narrative figures (Avraham, Eliezer, Yitzchak) appear as characters in the eitza story but are not given bechina equations in this Torah, so they are correctly absent from the bechina dataset.
